correspondence.component_scope: Southern El Cuy headward feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected headward route corresponds to the dashed blue drainage south of Cerro Encayapau, continuing east through the San Antonio del Cuy setting before turning north at the eastern margin of the plateau. The map shows several side feeders entering the same corridor. The correspondence is between drainage corridors, not the nearby road or administrative line.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary headwater-corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: No headwater hydronym established; Cerro Encayapau and San Antonio del Cuy are orientation features.

correspondence.component_scope: Barda Anocibar–El Cuy–La Punta corridor
correspondence.finding: The route follows mapped north-running drainage along the plateau escarpment and eastern side of Barda Anocibar to El Cuy, then northeast beside the main road toward La Punta. The named Cañadón San Salvador approaches from the west/southwest and is distinguished from the selected southern eastern-foot feeder. Cañadón Chico de El Cuy and Cañadón Grande de El Cuy are also separately depicted to the west. Nearby Laguna Chilena, Laguna Menuco and Laguna Verde are not treated as lakes traversed by the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Mapped headward-to-middle connection and distinct neighboring branches supported.
correspondence.name_scope: No nearby canyon or lagoon name is extended over the whole selected upper feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Bajo de la Mora–Currumil–Cañadón Soledad
correspondence.finding: The selected course turns east through Bajo de la Mora and the Currumil/Pozo de Currumil setting, then northeast along the mapped Cañadón Soledad drainage and low wetland belt south of Laguna Arancibia and Loma La Estrechura. Separate channels, lagoon features and southern tributary valleys are visible; the model is not interpreted as crossing every nearby open-water patch.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle course, lowland links and branch setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Original canyon-corridor label; not established as the hydronym of the entire selected river system.

correspondence.component_scope: Curacó–Cañadón El Salado lower canyon corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped drainage continues northeast into the Curacó setting and then east through the repeatedly labeled Cañadón El Salado corridor, past Loma Angostura and Loma La Jarancha. Original cartography provides the channel connection. The independently read field-research abstract confirms use of Cañadón El Salado as a named locality/canyon, but supplies no whole-route hydrographic identity.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower canyon route and its label supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Supported canyon name on a substantial selected component. It is not silently promoted to an officially registered river name or representative river-system hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Caita Co convergence and Salitral Bajo de Menucos
correspondence.finding: The El Salado drainage meets the separately labeled Caita Co corridor from the southwest and continues through the low channel belt into Salitral Bajo de Menucos. The selected generalized course is read within this convergence and northern saline-basin margin, not as an exact bank/vertex trace. The original overview explicitly shows the junction and eastward channel where the later high-resolution view contains a white rendering band.
correspondence.correspondence: Material tributary convergence and saline-basin entry supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Caita Co is a separate tributary-canyon label; Salitral Bajo de Menucos is a receiving saline feature, not a replacement river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Menucos–Puesto Las Salinas connector and actual Trapalcó terminal
correspondence.finding: A mapped dashed channel leaves the eastern/southeastern Menucos saline setting, continues southeast below the Puesto Trapalcó uplands, receives small side drainage and enters Salinas de Trapalcó near Puesto Las Salinas. The selected continuation follows this channel and finishes within the salina interior. Laguna del León, Laguna del Pozo and other southern basins are outside the selected terminal continuation.
correspondence.correspondence: Explicit basin connector and inland terminal supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Terminal salt-basin identity only; no river hydronym applied to the salina interior.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern opening and upper near-southward connector
correspondence.finding: The actually read southern portion of the 1995 national original, with its latitude and longitude graticule, places the northern opening and long near-southward connector within the broad southern Inland Ice interior, well between the exposed western and eastern coastal belts. That interior continues into the detailed southern sheet's northern overlap.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at bounded generalized regional/component scale.
correspondence.limits: National-scale cartography resolves the interior-ice setting; it does not supply a selected river trace or a local hydronym. Its surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs, bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments are distinct symbols, none treated as a river.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southward middle course into the southern ice-sheet interior
correspondence.finding: South of the 62°30′N sheet boundary, the graticule and ice-surface contours on the 2007 original place the selected southward steps in the continuous light-blue ice interior. Exposed terrain remains peripheral to this middle corridor. The national map supplies an overlapping regional view.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete bounded geographic setting read from original cartography.
correspondence.limits: Elevation contours are not channel traces, and the sheet does not establish a continuous natural-river name across the interior.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward interior bend and approach to the lower ice-margin belt
correspondence.finding: The small eastward and southeastward steps remain in the mapped ice interior and lead toward the more dissected southern ice-and-rock margin north of Johan Dahl Land. The original overlapping middle and southern windows cover the whole connection, rather than relying on an assumed connection between endpoint labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete bounded corridor context.
correspondence.limits: No selected lake chain, reservoir link or named river junction is established. This is not an assertion of current ice drainage or glacier-catchment membership.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower approach through the glacier-and-nunatak belt
correspondence.finding: The original southern map distinguishes ice from exposed bedrock islands and headlands north of Johan Dahl Land. The selected southward approach, short eastward steps and ensuing westward turn enter this mixed glacier/nunatak corridor near the headward side of Eqalorutsit Kangillit Sermiat. The lower setting is therefore not treated as uniform featureless ice, nor as an independently established through-river.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete ordinary component-scale ice/land correspondence.
correspondence.limits: No exact intersection with an individual rock boundary or bank is asserted. The map's local glacier name is not extended across the modeled route.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward glacier-tongue corridor and actual inner-fjord ending
correspondence.finding: The final westward and southwestward sequence approaches the mapped Eqalorutsit Kangillit Sermiat tongue, with exposed rock to either side and Johan Dahl Land on its eastern side. The actual ending is in that glacier-front/inner-head setting of Nordre Sermilik. The detailed map differentiates this inner fjord from the separate Qooqqup Sermia–Qooroq corridor east of Johan Dahl Land.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting read at generalized corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: This is a historical mapped terminal setting, not a surveyed river mouth, exact present ice front or current shoreline intersection. Neither the glacier nor receiving fjord name is accepted as the river group's name.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial Sierra de Valle Fértil mountain feeder and northern piedmont turn
correspondence.finding: The selected head lies in the narrow north-draining valley on the east side of the mountain divide, in the Campo Grande–Agua de la Laguna setting. Detailed contours and blue channel symbols show its northward course and the eastward bend below Mogote de Arriba. It joins the southeast-directed intermittent piedmont drainage south of the Los Baldecitos road sector. The nearby Quebrada del Rincón Grande and other ravine labels are not used as names for every selected headward part.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete generalized headward land/channel correspondence supported by actually read 100k cartography.
correspondence.name_scope: No separate hydronym for the initial selected feeder is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Balde del Rosario–Loma Negra alluvial route
correspondence.finding: The route continues southeast across the intermittent alluvial belt east of Balde del Rosario and south of Loma del Puesto, then alongside the Loma Negra/Portillo de Anguango setting. The San Antonio-side and Las Guardias-side drainages are visible in relation to the selected corridor. Their labels identify neighboring or incoming reaches and are not spread over the entire selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: Alluvial channel corridor and material neighboring/receiving drainage setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Upper reach names remain bounded to their labelled reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Médano Colorado–Barreal Atravesado–Usno-side passage
correspondence.finding: South of Médano Colorado the selected route follows the low intermittent/barreal corridor east of Usno and continues through the Colonia Los Valencianos/Baldes del Norte setting toward San Agustín. The maps distinguish Río Usno and the northern barreal approach. The plan's project text identifies Baldes del Norte as the place where Usno and Valle Fértil join; this is supporting prose, not a substitute for the inspected junction cartography.
correspondence.correspondence: Northern lowland approach and Usno–Valle Fértil junction setting supported at corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Do not call every northern feeder or Barreal Atravesado passage Río Usno or Río del Valle.

correspondence.component_scope: San Agustín receiving junction, reservoir distinction and named Río del Valle corridor
correspondence.finding: Original maps label Río del Valle on the branch entering from the western mountain valley and on the channel continuing east of San Agustín. The selected northern route joins the downstream valley rather than traversing the blue reservoir by the town. The river then bends southeast across the plain toward the El Naranjito setting. The plan uses Río del Valle and Río Valle Fértil and describes infiltration and only exceptional continuation to the salinas.
correspondence.correspondence: Named receiving river, selected junction and downstream bend supported; reservoir is on the other upstream branch.
correspondence.name_scope: Supports the representative downstream river identity, not a uniform name for all selected land/channel components.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Tumanas–Astica lower valley and fan junctions
correspondence.finding: The southeast-running named valley passes the El Naranjito setting and the mapped Las Tumanas distributary/fan corridor, then turns south alongside the Barreal Colorado/La Piconina–El Chacón lowland. Astica, Río Verde and Chucuma-side drainage approaches are depicted from the western mountain front. They are intermittent/distributary systems and not all shown as permanent single-channel confluences.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower trunk, alluvial fans and adjoining depression corridor supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Retain distinctions among tributary names, alluvial fans and the receiving lower valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Barreal de Chucuma and southern dry-depression connector
correspondence.finding: The detailed lower map shows a long chain of narrow bare/depressed surfaces through Campo Blanco, Barreal de Chucuma, La Morena and the Barreal de Mascasín establishment setting. The selected route continues south along that chain and turns southwest into the northern salina margin. The 250k map has no continuous blue stream for this entire lower interval. Its generalized seasonal connection is supported by the actually inspected 100k depression corridor together with the plan's exceptional-flood course statement.
correspondence.correspondence: Seasonal land/barreal continuation supported; continuous permanent surface flow is not asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Barreal de Chucuma is a component landform label, not a whole-system hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal inside Salinas de Mascasín
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the cross-hatched salina depression, passes south of the Marayes–Mascasín transport corridor and terminates inside it. The 100k map explicitly labels Salinas de Mascasín. Pampa del Gigantillo lies to the west/southwest and Mascasín station/town to the northeast. No downstream sea connection is depicted or inferred.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual endorheic terminal setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Receiving terminal salina identity only; not a river name or an official length claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern headward corridor and Summercove setting
correspondence.finding: Holm's mapped Wood River starts near the southern watershed edge west/southwest of Mankota, runs east south of that community, and bends north. This distinctive route corresponds to the selected upper corridor. WSA places Summercove Dam on Wood River south of Mankota.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous mapped headward corridor plus explicit primary prose identifying the on-river impoundment; no precise impoundment outline claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward trunk and Thomson Lake
correspondence.finding: The source maps follow the northward trunk into the elongated Thomson Lake setting south of Gravelbourg. WSA identifies Thomson Lake as the reservoir created by Lafleche Dam on Wood River; its southern tributaries remain separate streams.
correspondence.correspondence: Upper-river approach, through-reservoir passage and downstream continuation covered at corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Gravelbourg, western tributary arrivals and northeastern lower route
correspondence.finding: Holm Figure 3.1 follows the river beyond Thomson Lake through the Gravelbourg study sites toward Shamrock Park, then northeast. WSA Figure 1 and prose distinguish Notukeu and Wiwa creeks arriving from the west. Their names are not used for the selected trunk.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower main corridor and material western tributary setting observed; separate tributaries are contextual, not selected branch FIDs.

correspondence.component_scope: Chaplin diversion choice and Old Wives terminal
correspondence.finding: Holm's map shows a northward connection toward Chaplin Lake and the eastward channel entering Old Wives Lake. WSA describes the Chaplin connection as an engineered diversion. The selected continuation takes the Old Wives route and extends into the terminal lake setting. ECCC prose describes Old Wives as a closed terminal waterbody with no outlet streams and variable mudflats.
correspondence.correspondence: Terminal channel choice and receiving lake established. The selected interior lake line is not evidence of a separately named river channel or an outlet. ECCC's unavailable map image supplies no visual evidence.
